answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a stake-bonded identity registry. Before an agent earns, it locks a deposit in a transparent escrow, a crystal-clear bond rather than a hidden fee. If duplicate or forged credentials are detected, the bond is slashed, so each fake identity costs real capital. A mesa of independent verifiers audits claims, and a walnut-sized waiting period delays withdrawals, giving auditors time to catch fraud. Attack cost grows linearly with every extra identity, while honest agents reclaim their full bond.
